paper_metadata.title: Quantum Option Proﬁt and Loss Encoding for Risk Assessment

summary: The paper proposes a Quantum Option Profit and Loss Encoding (QOPLE) circuit and a Quantum Option Risk Assessment (QORA) model for estimating option Value‑at‑Risk using maximum‑likelihood amplitude estimation. In Qiskit simulations with up to n=7 sampling qubits, the quantum VaR estimates achieve <1% relative error compared with classical Monte Carlo (10,000 samples) while claiming a theoretical quadratic speedup (O(1/ε) vs O(1/ε²)) and a 15% reduction in ancilla qubits compared to phase‑estimation‑based QAE.

experiments.description: Quantum option risk assessment for European call options using QOPLE encoding and maximum-likelihood-based amplitude estimation, evaluated in Qiskit simulation across different sampling-qubit counts and two option parameter sets.

algorithm.variant: Maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) based amplitude estimation with Grover amplification and binary search for VaR
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Not applicable; no variational parameters. Amplitude amplification sequence is exponentially increasing, starting from f0=0.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Option expiration-price distribution is loaded into an n-qubit register as a discretized lognormal distribution; a comparator-based auxiliary qubit marks whether strike price K is exceeded; a second comparator marks whether payoff/PnL is below threshold l.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate VaR as the minimum l such that P[PT <= l] >= alpha, where PT = max(ST-K,0) for call options (and max(K-ST,0) for put options, though experiments use call options).
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Comparator-based thresholding and binary search over l; no penalty formulation.
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: At most 2n+1 for P and up to 3n+2 for V, as stated in the paper; MLE-based QAE reduces auxiliary-qubit needs relative to phase-estimation QAE.

problem_instance.description: European call option VaR estimation under a lognormal Black-Scholes-Merton price model.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Truncate option price distribution to three standard deviations around the mean; uniformly sample 2^n points; fit sampled prices to integer encoding (e.g., ST = 0.229*i + 1.209 for n=3 case).
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulation in IBM Qiskit; VaR estimated for two option instances; probability at each l measured three times and averaged; compare against classical Monte Carlo with 10,000 repeated samples; relative error reported versus classical result.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 repeated samples) for baseline comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Discretize lognormal option-price distribution; map prices to integer states; binary search over payoff threshold l.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Average three probability estimates per l; compute relative error against classical Monte Carlo VaR.

speedup_claims.conditions: for amplitude estimation / VaR estimation in the NISQ setting
speedup_claims.caveats: Claimed from O(1/epsilon^2) classical Monte Carlo to O(1/epsilon) quantum amplitude estimation; the paper states MLE preserves the quadratic speedup while reducing resource overhead.

speedup_claims.conditions: using MLE-based amplitude estimation instead of phase-estimation QAE
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper states this as a resource comparison; exact qubit counts are not fully enumerated in the text excerpt.
Reported in the resource comparison table discussion; exact table values are not provided in the excerpt.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/epsilon) for amplitude estimation; binary search adds O(log2((lmax-lmin)/epsilon)) iterations; L loading described as O(2^n) circuit complexity.
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: MLE reduces auxiliary qubits by at least 15% and controlled amplification operations by 3x versus QAE (as reported).
complexity_analysis.total_operations_classical: Monte Carlo requires O(1/epsilon^2) samples; 10,000 samples used in comparison plots.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: not estimated; experiments only use up to n=7 sampling qubits
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require large-scale fault‑tolerant quantum computers implementing amplitude estimation with deep Grover iterations and accurate lognormal state preparation; far beyond the ≤~23 logical qubits implied by the prototype circuit
limiting_factors: Only noiseless Qiskit simulations were performed
Problem sizes extremely small (n ≤ 7 discretization qubits)
State preparation of lognormal distributions requires nontrivial circuits with O(2^n) structure
No runtime or wall‑clock comparisons with classical Monte Carlo

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states 'using IBM Qiskit' and presents simulation results, but no real QPU/device name is given.
num_qubits reported as a range because the paper evaluates multiple sampling-qubit settings (n=3, n=4, and n=7).
Circuit depth is not numerically reported; only asymptotic circuit complexity and relative resource reductions are stated.
Authors claim theoretical quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo using amplitude estimation but only demonstrate small-scale noiseless simulations.
No empirical runtime advantage is demonstrated; comparisons are accuracy-based versus classical Monte Carlo.

experiments.description: Comparison between traditional QAE (phase-estimation-based amplitude estimation) and MLE-based amplitude estimation for evaluating the cumulative distribution function and VaR estimation accuracy.

algorithm.variant: Traditional QAE vs MLE-based amplitude estimation
algorithm.details: Evaluation performed with n=4 qubits discretizing the option distribution; amplification sequence parameter m varied (m ∈ {2,3,4,5}) for the MLE method.

key_results: MLE-based amplitude estimation achieves smoother and smaller estimation errors compared to QAE when sample size is small.
MLE reduces auxiliary qubits by at least 15% compared with phase-estimation-based QAE.
MLE reduces controlled amplification operations by approximately 3× relative to QAE.
Both approaches converge to O(1/M) estimation error asymptotically.
